- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes followed by model overcorrection, cap forecast growth after peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is rising, slow or reverse trend to avoid false bullish bias.  
- If true outcome diverges significantly from forecast early in horizon (e.g., first 5 days), adjust forecast downward if sentiment is weak or volatile.  
- Model tends to overestimate mean reversion in short-term (1-3 days) when sentiment is mixed; use sentiment-weighted smoothing for intermediate horizons.  
- For long-term (15+ days) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive, allow slight upward drift but cap at 10-15% above recent high to avoid inflationary bias.
